title: SCIM shadow-sync and idempotent reconcile for flaky SAML providers
creator: Maya Turner
description:
Problem: Several enterprise SAML identity providers intermittently return 5xxs or time out during SCIM user/group provisioning. These partial failures leave Redwood with dangling shadow accounts or out-of-sync group memberships. Symptoms: user shows active in IdP but missing in Redwood; deprovisioning requests sometimes race with re-provisioning; unclear audit trail linking SCIM request -> retry -> final state.

Goal: Implement a "shadow-sync" pattern plus an idempotent reconcile job to guarantee eventual consistency while preserving an auditable trail and bounded retry costs. Shadow-sync keeps a per-entity ordered operation log ("create/update/delete") and applies a durable tombstone marker on deletes; reconcile periodically drains the log with idempotent semantics. This approach decouples synchronous SCIM request handling from long-running recovery and avoids duplicate side-effects when providers retry.

Success criteria: 
- Reduce customer-facing inconsistency incidents by >90% for flaky provider windows.
- Median time to eventual consistency < 5 minutes under normal load, < 30 minutes under degraded provider behavior.
- All SCIM operations surface an audit reference ID tied into the platform audit log and console trace.

Design notes and tradeoffs: 
- We intentionally avoid immediate global locks because they hurt latency on common happy-path provision requests. Instead we record operations to a lightweight append-only store (implementation: Kafka topic or DynamoDB stream; prototype uses DynamoDB for simplicity).
- Tombstone markers for deletes are retained for a configurable TTL (default 30 days) to support undeletion workflows and audit queries; retention is configurable per-customer.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter and a capped maximum attempts; reconcile job will escalate to 'manual review' status when attempts exceed thresholds.
- Audit linking: every SCIM API response includes an audit_id; reconcile events attach the same audit_id so Console and logs can show the full lifecycle.

Alternatives considered: 
- Synchronous strong consistency via distributed locking: rejected due to increased latency and outage blast radius.
- Immediate single-queue retry in API path: simpler but risks repeated retries causing duplicate downstream side-effects and poor scaling for spikes.

Open questions: 
- Persistence backend selection across Private vs Hosted deployments (DynamoDB ok for hosted, postgresql/redis-backed queue for private).
- Exact TTL defaults and legal retention constraints for customers in regulated industries.

Rollout plan: 
1) Feature-flagged beta for a small set of customers (internal and two early enterprise customers) with enhanced telemetry.
2) Run reconcile at low cadence (60s) initially, increase as confidence grows.
3) Enable automatic tombstone cleanup and set retention policy defaults after security review.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Reconcile job could amplify load during IdP-wide outages. Mitigation: circuit-breaker on per-customer retry rate, progressive backoff and manual throttle controls in Console.
- Risk: Audit correlation missing if API times out before writing audit_id. Mitigation: make audit write synchronous before returning 202 to client; timeouts only on downstream provider calls.

Refer to attachments for design doc, prototype PR, metrics dashboard and runbook.
updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket created after paging incident where two enterprise customers reported missing users following SCIM provisioning failures. Initial triage points to provider timeouts and duplicate creates.

2025-02-18: Spike completed — prototype write-path implemented using DynamoDB streams and a small consumer. Local tests show idempotent create/update logic prevents dupes when request retried with same external id. Confluence design updated.

2025-02-22: Design review with Security and Product. Security requested explicit tomstone TTL controls and audit_id guarantees; Product asked for console visibility for pending reconcile items. Action: add per-customer TTL setting and audit correlation in API responses.
2025-02-24: Implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12345. Initial CI passes; some style feedback from reviewers (naming and extra unit tests).

2025-02-27: Load test on staging with injected IdP 503s. Result: eventual consistency achieved within 7 minutes at 95th percentile; reconcile queue growth capped with circuit-breaker. Noted increased DynamoDB costs during high retry window; Optimize batching to reduce writes.

2025-03-01: Security review scheduled for 2025-03-04. Preparing runbook for manual de-escalation and customer notifications. Next: address reviewer comments and add per-tenant retention UI in Console.
